title: Packaging Apps with Helm Charts
description: Package and deploy complex applications using Helm, the Kubernetes package manager.

data.text: **Helm** is the package manager for Kubernetes. It lets you define, install, and upgrade even the most complex Kubernetes applications using **charts** — packages of pre-configured Kubernetes resources. Think of Helm as `apt` or `npm`, but for Kubernetes.

terms.definition: A Helm package containing all the Kubernetes manifests and configuration for an application.
An instance of a chart running in a cluster — like running a package.
A YAML file that customizes a chart's templates during installation.
A collection of charts that can be shared and used by others.
A Go-template-based manifest file that gets rendered with values.

data.text: Managing raw YAML files for every environment quickly becomes unwieldy. You end up with dozens of files and manual find-and-replace. Helm solves this by parameterizing your manifests with values, so a single chart can work across development, staging, and production.

data.title: Scaffolding a Helm chart
data.content: Create a new chart and inspect its directory structure.
data.code:
helm create myapp

myapp/
  Chart.yaml
  values.yaml
  templates/
    deployment.yaml
    service.yaml
    _helpers.tpl

data.text: The `Chart.yaml` file contains metadata about the chart. The `values.yaml` file holds default configuration. The `templates/` directory contains the Kubernetes manifest templates.

data.title: Chart metadata
data.content: The Chart.yaml describes the chart and its dependencies.
data.code:
apiVersion: v2
name: myapp
version: 0.1.0
appVersion: "1.0"
description: A Helm chart for MyApp
keywords:
  - web
  - api
dependencies:
  - name: postgresql
    version: 15.x.x
    repository: https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami

data.title: Default chart values
data.content: Define configurable parameters that templates reference.
data.code:
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: myapp
  tag: "1.0"
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 80
resources:
  limits:
    cpu: 500m
    memory: 512Mi
  requests:
    cpu: 100m
    memory: 256Mi

data.title: Deployment template
data.content: Use Go-style template variables to make manifests configurable.
data.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: {{ .Release.Name }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: {{ .Release.Name }}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: {{ .Release.Name }}
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80

data.title: Helm lifecycle commands
data.content: Install, upgrade, and roll back Helm releases.
data.code:
# Install (or upgrade)
helm install myapp ./myapp
helm upgrade myapp ./myapp
helm upgrade --install myapp ./myapp

# Upgrade with custom values
helm upgrade --install myapp ./myapp -f values-prod.yaml

# Rollback
helm rollback myapp 1

# List and uninstall
helm list
helm uninstall myapp

data.title: Helm repos
data.text: You can also install charts from existing repositories, e.g., `helm install my-redis bitnami/redis`. Use `helm repo add` to register new repos and `helm search` to find charts.
Charts can declare dependencies on other charts, listed in `Chart.yaml`. Helm resolves and downloads them automatically, making it easy to compose complex applications like a web app with a database.

data.title: Package and deploy with Helm
data.description: Create, customize, and deploy a Helm chart.
steps: Run `helm create myblog` to scaffold a chart.
Customize `values.yaml` with your own image and replica count.
Check the release: `helm list` and `kubectl get pods`.
Modify a value in `values.yaml` and run `helm upgrade`.
Run `helm uninstall myblog` to clean up.
data.expectedOutcome: You've deployed a chart with Helm, customized its values, and performed a rolling upgrade.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes — charts package manifests and configuration together.
A chart has Chart.yaml metadata, values.yaml defaults, and template manifests.
Use `helm install` to deploy and `helm upgrade` to update with rolling changes.
Helm supports rollbacks, dependencies, and reusable repositories.
data.takeaway: Helm turns complex Kubernetes deployments into versioned, shareable packages.
